title.narrative: UNDP: The Sahel Resilience Project phase 2: DRR CC Adaptation for Resilience
UNDP: The Sahel Resilience Project phase 2: DRR CC Adaptation for Resilience

description.narrative:
The Sahel resilience project phase 1 and this phase 2 aims to build increased resilience to shocks and crisis in the Sahel (and Africa) by strengthen the policy and institutional capacities at regional and national levels to better manage multidimensional risks through device mechanisms that anticipate and respond to the challenges the region faces by enhancing the implementation of the Sendai Framework for disaster risk reduction (SFDRR). The Project's expected outcome is that Regional institutions and national governments institutionalize and domesticate risk-informed development planning, programming, and investment for resilience building. This will integrate risk reduction in planning and investment decisions. This is done through the following results (outputs):
Output 1: Increased capacity on tracking and monitoring progress on Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (SFDRR) and AU Programme of Action implementation in the Sahel region through enhanced data collection, analysis, and reporting systems
Output 2: Strengthened regional and multi-country regulatory, policy, and budgetary frameworks for translating disaster and climate data into risk-informed development
Output 3: Enhanced regional recovery and resilience-building processes that address underlying disaster and climate change risks and restore pathways to sustainable development in the Sahel countries
Output 4: Enhanced regional capacities for urban risk management
Output 5: Enhanced innovations and knowledge on risk-informed development through Regional Dialogue and South-South exchange
(i) Disaggregated climate and disaster risk information must be collected, analyzed and utilized to inform the planning and investment decisions made by the national governments and the society; (ii) A conducive policy environment must be in place to guide and enhance capacities of regional and national institutions in the Sahel to understand and translate disaster and climate risk information into decision making processes for development that leave no-one behind; (iii) Sahel regional institutions, national governments and community members have systems and mechanisms in place to manage future recovery processes in a manner that is effective and promotes long-term resilience building; and (iv) Urban areas, which are the powerhouse for economic development, have robust urban risk management systems to respond and adapt to the increasing climatic and disaster risks such that it offers itself as a sustainable engine of transformation.

Länderna i Sahel står inför multipla sammanlänkade chocker beroende på förändringar i klimatet som torka och översvämningar, markförstöring, matosäkerhet, ökad konfliktrisk och flyktingströmmar. Liksom i den första fasen syftar insatsen till att öka motståndskraften mot klimatchocker och kriser i Sahel (och Afrika) genom genomförandet av Sendai ramverket för katastrofriskreducering för stärkande av policies och den institutionella kapaciteten. Insatsen syftar till att nå resultat inom fem resultatmål: Ökad kapacitet i att följa upp genomförandet av Sendai Ramverket. och AUs program för genomförandet av Sendai ramverket genom datainsamlande, analys, rapporteringssystem 2) Ökad regional och multilands reglering, policy och budgetramverk, ramverk för att översätta katastrof- och klimatdata till risk informerad utvecklings planering och budgetarbete 3) Ökad regional återhämtningsförmåga och motståndskraft genom att bygga processer som inriktas på underliggande katastrof- och klimatförändringsrisker och att återställa möjligheter till en hållbar utveckling för länderna i Sahel. 4) Öka den regionala kapaciteten för uban katastrofriskreducering i Västafrika 5)Förbättrade innovation och ökad kunskap om riskinformerad utveckling genom regional dialog och Syd-syd utbyte.

The seven Sahel countries (Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria and Senegal) are facing multiple interlinked shocks and stressors: climate induced factors as recurrent droughts and flooding, land degradation, high levels of food insecurity and malnutrition, rising insecurity, unequal access to basic services, poorly integrated markets and displacement. As in its first phase the project aims to build increased resilience to climate induced shocks and crisis in the Sahel (and Africa) by enhancing the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (SFDRR) thus strengthen the policy and institutional capacities at regional and national levels to better manage multidimensional risks through device mechanisms that anticipate and respond to the challenges the region faces. The project aimed to achieve results by the five outputs: 1) Increased capacity on tracking and monitoring progress on Sendai Framework and AU Program of Action implementation through enhanced data collection, analysis and reporting system; 2) Strengthened regional and multicountry regulatory, policy and budgetary frameworks for translating disaster and climate data into risk informed development planning and budgeting; 3) Enhanced regional recovery and resilience building processes that address underlying disaster and climate change risks and restore pathways to sustainable development in the Sahel Countries; 4) Enhanced Regional Capacities for Urban Risk Management in West Africa; and 5) Enhanced innovations and knowledge on risk informed development through Regional Dialogue and SouthSouth exchange.

1. Implementation arrangements and expected outputs The Project aims to strengthen regional and national policy and institutional capacities for riskinformed development. It seeks to improve risk understanding, enhance anticipatory and response mechanisms, and integrate risk reduction in development planning and investments. The Projects Phase 2 focused on achieving the expected outcome of ensuring that both regional organizations and national governments are equipped to institutionalize and integrate riskinformed development planning and programming, and investment into resiliencebuilding frameworks in the face of multifaceted challenges, through the following outputs: Output 1: Increased capacity of tracking and monitoring progress on SFDRR and AU Programme of Action implementation in the Sahel region through enhanced data collection, analysis, and reporting systems. Output 2: Strengthened regional and multicountry regulatory, policy, and budgetary frameworks for translating disaster and climate data into riskinformed development. Output 3: Enhanced regional recovery and resiliencebuilding processes that address underlying disaster and climate change risks and restore pathways to sustainable development in the Sahel countries. Output 4: Enhanced regional capacities for urban risk management. Output 5: Enhanced innovations and knowledge on riskinformed development through Regional Dialogue and SouthSouth exchange.
A cost extension of the project was approved in 2025, extending the activities under Phase 2 of the project. Despite some delays , mainly in the work of the UNDP subcontracted partners, the contribution has achieved impressing results. Also the UNDP support to the AU in developing the AU Urban Resilience Project has been successful. Under a Service Procurement Agreement with the Swedish Meterological and Hidrological Institute (SMHI), capacity building and database development of a climate and early warning system is being developed within the project.
2. Social, climate change, and disaster context in the Sahel region Between June 2023 and September 2025, disasters and sociopolitical changes spotlighted the regions vulnerability. From a social perspective, the region continues to face heightened sociopolitical volatility. The January 2025 withdrawal of Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger from ECOWAS has challenged regional integration and institutional architecture. Simultaneously, the security situation has deteriorated, particularly in Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali and Niger. Armed violence escalated in Burkina Fasos eastern region in June July 2025. Mali saw terrorist activity, notably the coordinated 1 July 2025 assaults across seven localities Niono, Molodo, Sandaré, Kayes, Diboli, Nioro du Sahel, and Gogui which inflicted heavy casualties and destruction to both military and civilian populations. This volatile environment has exacerbated vulnerabilities, causing severe humanitarian and socioeconomic consequences: thousands of schools nearly 5,300 in Burkina Fasohave been closed, while markets and health facilities have become inoperable in several regions. Youth unemployment has exceeded 60 percent, heightening risks of exploitation and forced migration. Largescale displacement, including 800,000 Sudanese refugees in Chad, has pushed internally displaced persons (IDPs) in the region to 9.2 million as of 2025. This crisis is worsened by a nearly 20 percent decline in development assistance, disproportionately affecting programmes on womens education, health, and livelihoods. In Burkina Faso alone, development assistance cuts suspended nearly 45 percent of communityled womens empowerment projects, undermining local resilience. From a climate change and disaster perspective, the Sahel and West Africa persist as one of the regions most affected by climate change, facing recurrent droughts, floods, desertification, and land degradation. In 2024 alone, catastrophic floods impacted at least 16 countries in the region and seven million people in West and Central Africa (WACA). Chad, Niger, and Nigeria were hardest hit, with Maiduguri, Nigeria experiencing widespread destruction after the Alau Dam collapse in September 2024. Likewise, in 2025, flooding notably in Nigeria, Niger and Mauritania resulted in disrupted services, damage and loss. In addition, environmental stress has exacerbated competition over scarce natural resources such as water, pasture, and arable land, often contributing to local conflicts. 3. Results and achievements Within this implementation context, the Projects Phase 2 has continued to serve as a platform for regional organizations and national and local governments to address the complex interaction of systemic risks with the objective of bridging resilience gaps by strengthening capacities at the regional, national, and community levels to anticipate, prevent, absorb, adapt to, and recover from shocks and stresses. Examples include: -Strengthening regional capacity for integrated risk data management: Progress was made in strengthening regional risk information systems and early warning capabilities. This included establishment of a regional risk information platform, enhanced digital data collection and analysis, support to the implementation of the Africa MultiHazard Early Warning and Early Action System (AMHEWAS) programme, strengthened coordination and facilitation of knowledge exchange, and building conflict early warning capacity. - Strengthening policy and budgetary frameworks for riskinformed development: With support from the Project and the Climate Security Programme, ECOWAS developed, validated and adopted the Regional Resilience Strategy for West Africa (2024-2050).26 Aligned with Agenda 2063 and ECOWAS Vision 2050, the Strategy provides phased guidance to Member States and stakeholders on integrated, multisectoral resiliencebuilding across governance, economic, social, and environmental pathways. - Enhancing regional recovery preparedness: Strengthening institutional arrangements for effective recovery preparedness at regional and national levels is critical for resilience building. - Advancing urban resilience: For longterm investment in riskinformed urban development, the Projects Phase 2 continued reinforcing urban resilience at multiple levels, including the African Union Urban Resilience Program (AURP) - Establishing national disaster databases and leveraging academia in disaster response management - Strengthening nationalregional coordination on early warning and impactbased forecasting - Improving institutional and policy frameworks for disaster risk governance - Strengthening recovery at national level and urban resilience at local level
The contribution also include a Service Procurement Agreement with SMHI to provide technical assistance in setting up and train staff in weather forcasting, early warning, and climate database management
